items.title: NVIDIA / SkillSpector
items.summary: Security scanner for AI agent skills. Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, security risks, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and supply-chain risks in Claude Code, Codex, and MCP skills before you install them.
items.excerpt: # SkillSpector **Security scanner for AI agent skills.** Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, and security risks before installing agent skills. [![Python 3.12+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) ## Overview AI agent skills (used by Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, etc.) execute with implicit trust and minimal vetting. In the 31,132-skill analyzed subset of the research dataset, **26.1% of skills contain vulnerabilities** and **5.2% show likely malicious intent**. SkillSpector helps you answer: **"Is this skill safe to install?"** SkillSpector is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/), which scans, evaluates, and signs agent skills before publication. Skills that pass are published to the [NVIDIA skills catalog](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills). ## Documentation - **[Scan agent skills before installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/scanning-agent-skills)** — Hosted guide: when to scan, how to read a report, and how to gate installs. - **[Development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)** — Architecture, package layout, and how to extend the analyzer pipeline. - **[Analysis resource bounds](docs/ANALYSIS_RESOURCE_BOUNDS.md)** — Fail-closed bundle, parser, nested-artifact, ledger, and finding ceilings. - **[Pi extension](docs/PI_EXTENSION.md)** —…

items.summary: Upgrade your Claude Code setup with 8 free GitHub repos that fix what the agent can't do alone. In this Claude Code tutorial: Claude Code tips for 3D landing pages, real app testing, shorter replies and better designs. The AI coding tools that make coding with AI actually hold up. Build and deploy your own MCP app with Manufact for free at https://manufact.com/r/84WX7 Community with All Resources: https://ailabspro.io/?v=Ua0APTMVcb8 The Roundup, our daily newsletter covering the AI stories that matter. Join now: https://www.theroundup.so/ AI agents like Claude Code can build most of what you ask for, but there's still a lot they can't do on their own. People have built tools that fix those gaps, and we went through them to find the ones that actually hold up. These eight changed how we work, and they all work with Claude Code. This isn't about how to setup Claude Code from scratch. It's about what to add once you setup Claude Code and want better results. Every repo here is free to install, so this is a free Claude Code setup upgrade (you still need access to Claude Code itself). items.title: Tencent / BrowserSkill
items.summary: Let AI agents use your real, logged-in browser without interrupting your work. CLI + extension for browser automation across any shell-capable AI agent.
items.excerpt: # BrowserSkill Let AI agents use your browser without interrupting your work. English · 中文 **BrowserSkill** connects Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and other AI agents to your already logged-in browser. Need the agent to touch a tab you already have open? It must borrow that tab explicitly, return it when the task is done, and leave the rest of your browser alone. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db782c92-b1d4-4aae-a255-039675937a90 ## BrowserSkill Advantages - **Reuse real login state**: Agents can work with sites you are already signed into, without separate test accounts. - **Keep working uninterrupted**: browser tasks run in a separate, visible Agent Window, so you can keep using your own browser. - **Support any Agent**: any Agent that can call a shell can use BrowserSkill through the `bsk` CLI, with no lock-in to a specific model, Agent framework, or harness. - **Built-in human-in-loop**: when a task hits captcha, login, confirmation dialogs, or other human-only steps, the Agent can ask you to take over and then continue afterwards. Capture a long image in **Quick actions → Full-page screenshot**, or let an Agent use `bsk screenshot --session --full-page --out page.png`. See the [full-page screenshot guide](docs/long-screenshot.md) for page support, cancellation and export. ## Runtime Environment BrowserSkill has two local runtime pieces: the `bsk` CLI/daemon and the browser extension. | Runtime…

items.title: You Built Your AI Second Brain. Now What? (Here's How to Evolve It)
items.summary: An AI second brain works for one person. Once a whole team needs one, that stops being true. And you can't simply just build a "bigger" second brain. The team needs a different layer underneath, and this video is about that layer - the team brain. I show you how the team brain works: how information from chat platforms, repos, and docs goes in a single table, how search over that table works, how every row gets labeled, and how the database enforces those labels on every read for security and permissions. Then your coding agent queries it over MCP with its own token, and your own second brain keeps its memory system and personality on top! I use Oracle AI Database to show it, but the structure works with the tools you already have. items.title: My NEW FAVORITE Skill - Claude Code Drives My Whole Computer (Better Computer Use)
items.summary: I'm obsessed with computer use right now. My coding agent drives my computer every single day, and I don't use any sort of tool for it! No Codex computer use, no GitHub repo, no harness. The LLMs are powerful enough to drive the screen entirely on their own now reliably, so all it took was one super simple skill. That simplicity is why I love it even though I used to be quite opposed to computer use. It's lightweight, easy to customize, and when it makes a mistake the fix is one more rule in the skill. It sets up my machine in the morning, stages my demos, tests desktop apps, and drives other agent sessions. items.title: BMAD's Founder on the Future of AI Coding (And the Slop Apocalypse)
items.summary: There's a slop apocalypse coming, and it's not broken AI generated code crashing everything in production. It's the quiet kind: comments drift out of sync with what the code actually does, nobody goes back and refactors what the agent wrote, and over time that's what makes the coding agent slower and more expensive to work with (the real failure mode). That's Brian Madison's read on where AI coding is headed, and a couple days ago I sat down with him to dig into it - why "human on the loop" beats full automation, what's coming in BMAD v7, and how his framework and my own landed on almost the same philosophy independently.
